query: Research database design alternatives for a reusable PHP/Laravel commerce library, using primary official documentation and public source code. Compare Magento/Adobe Commerce EAV typed attributes, Sylius product options and attributes, Lunar Laravel field types and attributes, Bagisto attribute values, and Shopify metafields/metaobjects. Distinguish documented public API/domain concepts from unknown proprietary physical database schema. Focus on product vs variant vs sellable SKU vs inventory item, global/locale/channel scope, typed scalar/enum/multiselect/measurement/reference values, schema versioning and validation, variant combinations and uniqueness, faceted search/indexing, JSON/JSONB vs typed EAV vs relational core. Give a trade-off matrix, concrete failure scenarios, unresolved questions, and exact official/source URLs supporting each factual claim. Do not invent table names for SaaS. Suggest 2-3 alternative architectures rather than declaring a universal ideal.

Research inventory and reservation correctness for a modular PHP/Laravel commerce library. Use primary official sources from Adobe Commerce Inventory Management reservations/source selection, Shopify InventoryItem/InventoryLevel and quantities, Sylius inventory, and PostgreSQL locking/isolation documentation. Explain warehouse vs location vs sales channel vs stock/sales pool, physical quantity vs reserved vs available vs committed, reservation expiration and compensation, checkout/payment timing, concurrent checkout oversell prevention, idempotency, transfers in transit, returns/quarantine, lot/serial/bundle extension boundaries. Compare append-only movement ledger plus projection versus mutable balance with audit ledger, showing one transaction-level concurrency protocol and failure/recovery scenarios. Distinguish source facts from proposed design and do not infer proprietary SaaS physical schemas. Include exact primary URLs and note any contradictory terminology across systems.

Research deterministic pricing, promotions, coupons, and extension architecture for a reusable PHP/Laravel commerce package. Compare primary documentation/source for Sylius promotion rules/actions/processors and plugins, Lunar discounts/cart pipelines/pricing, Bagisto cart rules and Concord model proxies, Adobe Commerce sales rules and extension points, Shopify discount combinations/functions/allocations. Analyze price context (currency/channel/customer/quantity/time), integer or decimal money and rounding allocation, priority/stacking/exclusivity, free shipping vs item/order discounts, usage-limit races, coupon reservations and redemption lifecycle, immutable order snapshots and refunds. Compare typed contracts/registries/pipelines/domain events versus arbitrary Eloquent model replacement and synchronous callbacks. Give explicit invariants, reentrancy/ordering hazards, transaction boundaries, plugin compatibility/versioning, and pragmatic module boundaries. Supply exact official URLs/public source links for factual claims and clearly label design proposals.

Act as a critical architecture reviewer researching a maximally flexible reusable PHP/Laravel commerce package. Ground comparisons in primary official sources and public code of Sylius, Lunar, Bagisto, Magento/Adobe Commerce, Shopify, and optionally Vendure/Saleor/Medusa. Challenge the idea of one ideal universal schema. Analyze B2B quotes, subscriptions, digital goods, services, configurable/bundle products, multi-warehouse transfers, multivendor marketplace, taxes, refunds and partial fulfillment as stress cases. Which concepts should be stable relational core, optional modules, external integrations or plugins? Explain bounded-context ownership, avoiding duplicated source of truth, order-line historical snapshots, tenant vs shop vs channel and account/user ownership. Present 3 plausible architecture profiles with explicit exclusions, migration paths, worst failure modes and smallest vertical slices that can falsify design assumptions. Include exact primary/source URLs, separate facts/inferences, and do not assert private SaaS database structure.
